 Five Days of Diwali 2026: Dates, Meaning and Rituals
 Diwali 2026 runs from Dhanteras on 6 November to Bhai Dooj on 11 November. Day-wise dates, tithi, significance and rituals for all five days, with the Lakshmi Puja muhurat.
 By Sadrish Dabadi 12 min Read 
 Diwali, the festival of lights, is celebrated over five days across India and by Indian communities around the world. The five days begin with Dhanteras and end with Bhai Dooj , and each day has its own story, its own ritual and its own tithi on the Hindu lunar calendar. In 2026 the festival runs from Friday, 6 November to Wednesday, 11 November , with the main day of Lakshmi Puja on Sunday, 8 November .
 Quick Answer
 Diwali 2026 is a five-day festival that begins with Dhanteras on Friday, 6 November 2026 and ends with Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, 11 November 2026 . The main day, Diwali or Lakshmi Puja, falls on Sunday, 8 November 2026 , on Kartika Krishna Amavasya, and the puja is done in Pradosh Kaal after sunset. Govardhan Puja is on Tuesday, 10 November 2026 .
 Key Facts at a Glance
 Diwali 2026: Sunday, 8 November 2026
 Tithi of the main day: Kartika Krishna Amavasya
 Dhanteras 2026: Friday, 6 November 2026 (Kartika Krishna Trayodashi)
 Naraka Chaturdashi 2026: Saturday, 7 November 2026 (Kartika Krishna Chaturdashi)
 Govardhan Puja 2026: Tuesday, 10 November 2026 (Kartika Shukla Pratipada)
 Bhai Dooj 2026: Wednesday, 11 November 2026 (Kartika Shukla Dwitiya)
 Lakshmi Puja muhurat (New Delhi): about 05:54 PM to 07:50 PM IST; it follows local sunset, so it differs by city
 Length: five days, from Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj
 Also called: Deepavali, Deepawali, Festival of Lights
 Main deities: Lakshmi and Ganesha on Diwali; Krishna on Govardhan Puja; Yamraj and Dhanvantari on Dhanteras

 The Five Days of Diwali 2026 at a Glance 
 Day Date in 2026 Festival Tithi What is done 
 Day 1 Fri, 6 November Dhanteras Kartika Krishna Trayodashi Homes and shops are cleaned, gold, silver or new utensils are bought, and a lamp is lit for Yamraj outside the door. 
 Day 2 Sat, 7 November Naraka Chaturdashi / Choti Diwali Kartika Krishna Chaturdashi Oil bath before sunrise, ubtan, fresh clothes and rows of diyas; in Tamil Nadu and Goa this morning is the main Deepavali. 
 Day 3 Sun, 8 November Diwali / Lakshmi Puja Kartika Krishna Amavasya Lakshmi and Ganesha puja in the evening, rangoli at the entrance, diyas in every room, sweets and gifts. 
 Day 4 Tue, 10 November Govardhan Puja / Annakut Kartika Shukla Pratipada A hill of cow dung is made and worshipped, a mountain of food (Annakut) is offered to Krishna. 
 Day 5 Wed, 11 November Bhai Dooj Kartika Shukla Dwitiya Sisters apply tilak and aarti to their brothers and pray for their long life; brothers give gifts. 
 The dates above follow the tithis of the panchang. In 2026 the Pratipada tithi begins on the afternoon of 9 November, so the panchang keeps Govardhan Puja and the Gujarati new year on 10 November – some websites list 9 November instead, which is why the two dates are seen side by side. A puja muhurat can also differ by a few minutes from city to city, so check a local panchang for the exact window.
 Why the Diwali Date Changes Every Year 
 Diwali is fixed by the tithi, not by the calendar. It is celebrated on Kartika Krishna Amavasya , the new moon of the lunar month of Kartika. The Hindu lunar year runs about eleven days shorter than the solar year, so that Amavasya moves, and in 2026 it falls on 8 November. Lakshmi Puja is done in Pradosh Kaal , the window that begins after sunset; because that window is measured from local sunset, the muhurat printed for one city will not match another.
 Day 1 – Dhanteras: Friday, 6 November 2026 
 Tithi: Kartika Krishna Trayodashi. Dhanteras, also called Dhantrayodashi, is the first day of the festival and is dedicated to wealth, health and preparation. According to the Puranas, Dhanvantari , the physician of the gods and the source of Ayurveda, came out of the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) holding the pot of amrita on this day. The evening is also linked to Yamraj, and a lamp called Yam Deep is lit outside the house to ask for protection from untimely death.
 Homes and shops are cleaned, entrances are decorated with rangoli and small footprints of Lakshmi, and families buy gold, silver, steel utensils or a new vehicle. In the evening, Lakshmi and Kuber are worshipped and the first diyas of the festival are lit.
 Clean the house and the shop, and place a rangoli at the entrance.
 Buy something in metal – gold, silver, steel or a new utensil – as a symbol of prosperity.
 In the evening, light a lamp facing south outside the door for Yamraj.
 Worship Lakshmi and Kuber with a diya, sweets and a short mantra.
 Mantra: Om Dhanvantaraye Namah (ॐ धन्वंतरये नमः). Read more about the day in the essence of Dhanteras .
 Day 2 – Naraka Chaturdashi or Choti Diwali: Saturday, 7 November 2026 
 Tithi: Kartika Krishna Chaturdashi. The second day marks the victory of Krishna over the demon Narakasura , who had taken 16,000 women captive and troubled the three worlds. Krishna, helped by Satyabhama, killed him and freed the women, and the day is celebrated as the end of that fear. In Gujarat the same day is Kali Chaudas , when the house is cleaned of negative energy before Lakshmi Puja.
 The traditional ritual is an oil bath before sunrise, with sesame oil and ubtan, followed by fresh clothes and rows of diyas. In Tamil Nadu and Goa the main Deepavali celebration happens on this morning, not on the next evening – the day begins with the oil bath and a sweet called lehiyam before sunrise.
 Bathe before sunrise with oil and ubtan; in many homes the eldest member applies oil first.
 Wear new clothes and light diyas along the walls, windows and courtyard.
 Make a small offering of sweets and, in some regions, break a bitter fruit to mark the end of trouble.
 Clean the kitchen and the puja room so the house is ready for the main day.
 Mantra: Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya (ॐ नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय). Read the story in Dhanteras and Naraka Chaturdashi .
 Day 3 – Diwali or Lakshmi Puja: Sunday, 8 November 2026 
 Tithi: Kartika Krishna Amavasya. This is the main day of the festival and the darkest night of the lunar month, which is why it is lit with the most lamps. For most of North India it marks the return of Rama to Ayodhya after fourteen years of exile and the defeat of Ravana; the people of Ayodhya lit lamps to welcome him home, and that is the origin of the row of lights.
 In the evening, Lakshmi , the goddess of wealth, is worshipped with Ganesha , the remover of obstacles. In Gujarat shopkeepers open new account books on this day (Chopda Pujan); in Bengal the same night is Kali Puja ; for Sikhs it is Bandi Chhor Divas , the day Guru Hargobind Sahib reached Amritsar after his release from Gwalior fort.
 The puja is done in Pradosh Kaal. For New Delhi in 2026 that window is about 05:54 PM to 07:50 PM IST; it follows local sunset, so use your own city’s panchang. Keep the house clean, light diyas in every room, leave one at the entrance and one near the tulsi plant, and offer lotus flowers, sweets and fruits.
 Mantra: Om Shreem Mahalakshmyai Namah (ॐ श्रीं महालक्ष्म्यै नमः). More in Lakshmi mantras to chant and rangoli and toran in Diwali .
 Day 4 – Govardhan Puja and Annakut: Tuesday, 10 November 2026 
 Tithi: Kartika Shukla Pratipada. The fourth day recalls the story of Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan on his little finger to shelter the people of Braj from the storm sent by Indra. To thank him, the people of Braj began to worship the hill and the cattle instead of the rain god, and the day became a festival of gratitude for nature and for food.
 Families make a small hill of cow dung or clay, decorate it, and offer it food and flowers. The Annakut – literally a mountain of food – is prepared and offered to Krishna before the family eats. In Maharashtra the same tithi is Bali Pratipada , which marks the return of King Bali, and in Gujarat the new year ( Bestu Varas ) is celebrated on this Pratipada, on 10 November 2026.
 Make and decorate a Govardhan hill from clay or cow dung, and worship it with diyas.
 Prepare Annakut – a large spread of food – and offer it before the family eats.
 In Maharashtra, worship King Bali and take the customary blessing from elders.
 Feed the cows and other animals before the family meal.
 Mantra: Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya . The full story is in Govardhan Puja and Annakut .
 Day 5 – Bhai Dooj: Wednesday, 11 November 2026 
 Tithi: Kartika Shukla Dwitiya. The last day celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. The story is of Yamuna , who welcomed her brother Yama , the god of death, with a tilak and a meal, and in return he promised that any brother who receives this tilak from his sister will not be troubled by untimely death.
 Sisters apply a tilak of roli and rice, do aarti with a lamp and pray for their brothers long life; brothers give gifts and promise to protect their sisters. The same day is called Bhau Beej in Maharashtra, Bhai Phonta in Bengal and Bhai Tika in Nepal.
 Prepare a tilak of roli, rice and sandalwood, and a small aarti thali.
 Sisters apply the tilak and do aarti, then offer sweets and a coconut.
 Brothers give a gift and a promise of protection.
 Families end the festival with a shared meal.
 Which of the Five Days Is the Main Diwali? 
 The third day is the main Diwali. It falls on Kartika Krishna Amavasya, and the Lakshmi Puja on its evening is the puja most families plan for weeks. Dhanteras and Naraka Chaturdashi prepare for it, and Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj close the festival. If a family can celebrate only one day, it is 8 November 2026 in most of India; in Tamil Nadu and Goa the main Deepavali morning is 7 November.
 Lakshmi Puja at Home: 8 Simple Steps 
 Clean the house and make a rangoli at the entrance, with small footprints of Lakshmi at the door.
 Set a clean altar with Lakshmi and Ganesha, and place a kalash with water, mango leaves and a coconut.
 Wash the idols, offer fresh clothes or a red cloth, and light a diya with ghee.
 Light diyas in every room, at the entrance, near the tulsi plant and in the puja room.
 Take a sankalp – state your name and the reason for the puja – then invoke Ganesha first.
 Offer lotus or marigold flowers, sweets, fruits and a coconut to Lakshmi and Ganesha.
 Chant the Lakshmi mantra or the Shri Suktam, and then do the aarti with the family.
 Distribute the prasad, light the last lamps, and leave the house lit through the night.
 The Same Five Days, Different Names 
 Diwali is one festival with many local names. The tithis are the same, but the customs and the words change from state to state, and that is why the same night can be Lakshmi Puja in one house and Kali Puja in another.
 Region What the five days are called there 
 North India Dhanteras, Choti Diwali, Diwali, Govardhan Puja, Bhai Dooj 
 Gujarat Dhanteras, Kali Chaudas, Diwali (with Chopda Pujan for account books), Bestu Varas or new year, Bhai Beej 
 Maharashtra Dhanatrayodashi, Narak Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Pujan, Bali Pratipada, Bhau Beej 
 Tamil Nadu and South India Deepavali is celebrated mainly on Naraka Chaturdashi, with the oil bath before sunrise 
 West Bengal Kali Puja is held on the night of Diwali; the five days are still called Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj 
 Nepal The same days are part of Tihar, which ends with Bhai Tika 
 Sikh tradition Bandi Chhor Divas, marking the release of Guru Hargobind Sahib from Gwalior fort 
 Religious and Cultural Significance of Diwali 
 Diwali is celebrated in honour of Lakshmi , the goddess of wealth and prosperity, and it is believed that she blesses her devotees with good fortune on this night. Business owners treat Diwali as an auspicious time to start new ventures and open new account books. The festival is also a family occasion – houses are cleaned and decorated, sweets are exchanged, and gifts carry gratitude rather than obligation.
 The festival is not only Hindu. Jains mark the day when Lord Mahavira attained moksha, Sikhs remember Guru Hargobind Sahib’s release, and in Bengal the night is given to Kali. Read more about how the festival is kept in different parts of the country in Diwali of North India and South India .
 An Eco-Friendly and Safe Diwali 
 Over the years Diwali has become linked with air and noise pollution from firecrackers, and with accidents caused by unsafe handling. The safer way to keep the festival is also the older way: light diyas and lamps instead of crackers, use LED lights, make rangoli with natural colours, and keep the celebration inside the family.
 Choose clay diyas and LED lights over crackers.
 Use natural rangoli colours, flowers or rice flour instead of chemical powders.
 Keep a bucket of water and a first-aid box ready if any crackers are used.
 Keep pets indoors – the noise is far harder on them than on people.
 Avoid plastic decorations and dispose of flowers and diyas responsibly.
 Frequently Asked Questions 
 When is Diwali in 2026?
 Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, 8 November 2026, on Kartika Krishna Amavasya. Lakshmi Puja is performed on the evening of that day, in Pradosh Kaal after sunset.
 What are the five days of Diwali in 2026?
 The five days are Dhanteras on Friday 6 November, Naraka Chaturdashi on Saturday 7 November, Diwali on Sunday 8 November, Govardhan Puja on Tuesday 10 November and Bhai Dooj on Wednesday 11 November 2026.
 Which day of Diwali is the main day?
 The third day, Diwali or Lakshmi Puja, is the main day. It falls on Kartika Krishna Amavasya, the new moon night, when homes are lit with diyas and Lakshmi and Ganesha are worshipped in the evening.
 When is Dhanteras in 2026?
 Dhanteras, the first day of the festival, falls on Friday, 6 November 2026, on Kartika Krishna Trayodashi. It is considered the most auspicious day of the year to buy gold, silver, utensils or a new vehicle.
 What is Naraka Chaturdashi and why is it called Choti Diwali?
 Naraka Chaturdashi is the second day, on Saturday 7 November 2026. It marks the day Krishna killed the demon Narakasura and freed 16,000 captive women. Because it comes one day before the main Diwali, it is called Choti Diwali, and in Tamil Nadu and Goa the main Deepavali celebration happens on this morning.
 When are Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj in 2026?
 Govardhan Puja falls on Tuesday, 10 November 2026, on Kartika Shukla Pratipada. Bhai Dooj falls the next day, Wednesday, 11 November 2026, on Kartika Shukla Dwitiya.
 What is the Lakshmi Puja muhurat on Diwali 2026?
 Lakshmi Puja is done in Pradosh Kaal, the window that begins after sunset on 8 November 2026. For New Delhi it runs from about 05:54 PM to 07:50 PM IST. The window follows local sunset, so the time differs from city to city.
 Why is Diwali celebrated on a different date every year?
 Diwali follows the Hindu lunar calendar. It is celebrated on Kartika Krishna Amavasya, and because the lunar year is about eleven days shorter than the solar year, that Amavasya moves on the Gregorian calendar. This is why Diwali falls on 8 November in 2026 and on a different date in other years.
 Diwali is a festival of light, family and gratitude. Whether you keep all five days or only the main Lakshmi Puja, the meaning stays the same – light a lamp , share something sweet, and make room for the people who matter.
